subject: Maths
central_question: How do powers and exponents describe multiplicative growth, simplify repeated multiplication and help represent extremely large or small numbers?
in_scope_units: Paper-folding thought experiment and repeated doubling of thickness.
Exponential or multiplicative growth in stories such as the shining stones, magical pond and combinations.
Comparison of linear additive growth with exponential multiplicative growth.
Meaning of powers and exponent notation, including zero and negative exponents.
Laws of exponents for multiplication, division and powers of powers.
Powers of 10 and comparison of very large quantities.
Estimation and modelling activities involving large numbers and assumptions.
banned_topics: Compound interest formulas not present in the chapter.
Exponential equations requiring algebraic solution methods.

known_pitfalls.claim: Exponential growth adds the same amount at every step.
known_pitfalls.correction: Exponential growth multiplies by the same factor; linear growth adds the same amount.
For the same nonzero base, aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ.
A power raised to a power gives (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ.

known_pitfalls.claim: Any expression of the form x × 10ⁿ is in standard scientific notation.
known_pitfalls.correction: In standard scientific notation, 1 ≤ x < 10 and n is an integer.

recommended_example_progression: Use the opening paper-folding table with initial thickness 0.001 cm to model doubling.
Compare the 46 folds with the linear 20 cm ladder-step model to the Moon.
Use the chapter summary examples to practise each exponent law.
Use the chapter's estimation questions to model a large real-world quantity with stated assumptions.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Figure it Out and Math Talk tasks are distributed across the chapter, followed by a summary of exponential growth, exponent laws and scientific notation.
